summary: Columbia Co., WA DNR wooden tower built about 1960-62 (sources differ), removed 1996; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden DNR tower with a cab, replacing an L-4 tower of the 1940s
facts.status_note: The tower was removed in 1996. No source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: L-4 tower in the 1940s; no exact year given.
40-foot wooden DNR tower built about 1960 per the register and Firelookout.com; WillhiteWeb says around 1962.
A survey crew set a station on top of the tower, described as a 10-foot square wood house on a 4-legged wooden tower, about 75 feet overall.
March 1970 newspaper item: station broken into three times; damage and value of articles estimated at $460.
Registered in the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on December 17, 2012.

corrections.why: The cited pages describe a 40-foot wooden tower, about 12.2 m. Nothing read supports the brief's 3.0 m. The 1963 survey gives about 75 feet overall; see resolved_conflicts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com give a 40-foot tower. The 1963 survey description, as quoted by WillhiteWeb and the Washington lookouts site, gives an overall height of about 75 feet. No source explains the gap, so the fact uses the 40-foot figure.
The register and Firelookout.com date the tower to about 1960. WillhiteWeb says around 1962, and the Washington lookouts site quotes a 1962-64 biennial report describing a replacement.

Most pages name the Washington DNR. A 1970 newspaper item, quoted by WillhiteWeb, places the station near Dayton in the Umatilla National Forest and says it was maintained cooperatively with the state DNR.
Firelookout.com puts the site four miles east of Dayton. The 1963 survey description puts its station five miles east-southeast of Dayton.

notes_for_editor: No staffing is named in these sources, so none is recorded. Access is omitted because no source gives it. The NGS station (PID RZ1694) is named on the Washington lookouts page; its datasheet was not read. A search hit about a Thorn Point lookout in the Los Padres (California) is a different site and was excluded. The height fact follows the 40-foot figure while the 75-foot survey figure stays a stated conflict.
